results.content: HTTPS wraps normal HTTP traffic inside TLS, so the client and server first authenticate each other (the server via its certificate) and then negotiate a shared session key using asymmetric cryptography. All data is then encrypted and integrity-checked with that symmetric key, so eavesdroppers can't read the content and anyone tampering with it in transit is detected.
